title: Crystal Indexing
description: Every peak of a diffraction pattern is one family of lattice planes, named by three whole numbers (h k l), and their spacing in a cubic crystal is the cube's edge over √(h² + k² + l²). Not every family shows: in a body centred or face centred lattice, waves from the extra atoms cancel some reflections exactly, and which ones are missing tells you the lattice. Indexing a pattern is reading a crystal's structure from its fingerprint. Unlocks the Laue Goniometer.

puzzle.goal: In a cubic crystal of edge a, the planes (h k l) are spaced d = a/√(h² + k² + l²). Write d.
puzzle.name: Cubic plane spacing
puzzle.ask: Find d in ångströms for silicon, a = 5.431 Å, planes (@{h} 1 1).
puzzle.method: The plane (h k l) cuts the axes at a/h, a/k and a/l; its distance from the origin is one over the length of (h, k, l)/a.
